name: Segmentation
ess: Break it into independent pieces — and make the pieces smaller.
subs: Divide an object into independent parts
Make it easy to take apart
Increase the degree of fragmentation
mfg: Modular tooling and fixtures instead of one dedicated machine
Sectional conveyor that can be reconfigured
Granulated or powdered feedstock instead of solid blocks
svc: Split a 40-question onboarding form into six short screens that each save on completion
Replace the annual appraisal with short weekly check-ins
Break one general enquiry queue into independent skill-based lanes so a slow case cannot block a fast one
Sell insurance or software as separable modules rather than one all-or-nothing bundle
Divide a year-long transformation into fortnightly slices that each deliver something usable
ask: What is the smallest useful unit of this service — and could we deliver just that?
Which step could run entirely on its own, without waiting for the others?
Could the customer receive part of the value before the rest is finished?

name: Taking out
ess: Extract the one troublesome part — or extract only the part you actually need.
subs: Separate an interfering part or property
Single out the only necessary part or property
mfg: Site the noisy compressor outside the production hall
Move inspection out of the line into a dedicated cell
svc: Take identity verification out of the branch appointment and do it in the app beforehand
Remove the single approval step that causes most of the delay, and control it by sampling instead
Route the small number of genuinely angry callers to a specialist team so they are not queued behind routine enquiries
Extract the 'advice' part of a professional service and sell it separately from the 'processing' part
Strip the one legally required paragraph out of a long letter nobody reads
ask: Which single element causes most of the trouble — can it be removed, relocated or done elsewhere?
What property do we actually need here, without the thing that currently carries it?
If this step vanished tomorrow, what would genuinely break?

name: Local quality
ess: Stop treating everything the same. Let each part do its own job, in its own best conditions.
subs: Change from uniform to non-uniform structure
Change the environment so each part is in the best conditions for it
Make each part perform a different, useful function
mfg: Harden only the surfaces that actually wear
Local cooling at the cutting point rather than chilling the whole machine
svc: Set different service levels by case type rather than one target for everything, so the average stops hiding both the fast and the stuck
Give complex cases a different route, a different SLA and a different skill set from simple ones, instead of one process for all
Vary branch opening hours by local footfall rather than a national standard
Tailor the call script to what you already know about that customer's history
Put the strongest coach on the shift that struggles, not evenly across all shifts
Different induction depth for a contractor, a graduate and an experienced hire
ask: Where are we treating everything identically when it plainly is not identical?
Which 10% of cases deserve a completely different process?
Is each part of this team or system in the conditions that suit it best?

name: Asymmetry
ess: Where symmetry is costing you, deliberately make the two sides different.
subs: Replace a symmetrical form with an asymmetrical one
If already asymmetrical, increase the asymmetry
mfg: A connector keyed so it can only be inserted one way
Asymmetric hopper that stops material bridging
svc: Refund instantly below a threshold, review above it — rather than one policy for every amount
Staff heavily on Monday morning and lightly on Friday afternoon instead of an even rota
Build deliberate one-way doors into a process — after this point there is no going back — to kill rework loops
Give new customers a different (richer) contact model from established ones
Make it very easy to join and deliberately deliberate to cancel — or the reverse, as a trust signal
ask: Where is 'fair and equal treatment' actually just uniformity that costs us?
What if the two sides of this exchange were not mirror images?
Which direction of flow should be easy, and which should be hard?

name: Merging
alias: Do it all in one go
ess: Bring like things together, or make operations happen at the same moment.
subs: Bring identical or related objects closer together, or merge them
Make operations parallel, or contiguous in time
mfg: Multi-spindle head drilling every hole in one pass
Batch heat treatment of a full trolley rather than one part at a time
svc: Pool the queues, not just the tasks: one queue served by everyone beats separate queues that idle at different rates while work waits in the next one
One hospital visit that combines bloods, scan and consultation instead of three separate trips
Merge the identity checks of three products into a single customer check reused across all of them
Run the credit check and the property search in parallel rather than in sequence
One field visit that services, inspects and quotes in the same appointment
ask: What is queueing separately that could queue together?
What does the customer currently do or receive several times that could happen once?
Which two steps could happen in the same moment rather than one after the other?
Where are we visiting, checking or asking twice?

name: Universality
ess: Make one thing do several jobs, so other things can be deleted.
subs: Make an object perform multiple functions
Eliminate the need for other objects
mfg: A pallet that is also the retail display unit
A single fixture that locates, clamps and gauges
svc: One record that serves intake, assessment and audit, instead of three that have to be reconciled afterwards
A single intake channel that routes by the content of the request rather than a separate route per product
The delivery visit also collects returns and takes the meter reading, so one movement does three jobs
The invoice doubles as the warranty certificate and the returns label
The booking confirmation is also the entry pass and the receipt
ask: What else could this person, document or touchpoint do while they are already here?
What could we delete entirely because something else now covers it?
Which single asset is nearest to doing two jobs already?

name: Nested doll
ess: Put one thing inside another, rather than beside it.
subs: Place one object inside another, and that inside a third
Pass one part through a cavity in another
mfg: Telescoping mast or nested packaging that ships flat
Tooling stored inside the machine it serves
svc: Embed training inside the actual work — the guidance appears in the system at the moment of the decision
Put the feedback question inside the confirmation screen instead of emailing a survey later
Nest a specialist opinion inside the GP appointment by video, rather than a separate referral
Deliver your service inside a partner's app where the customer already is
Fold the compliance check into a step the customer wants to do anyway
ask: Where could this be embedded inside something the customer is already doing?
What could nest inside capacity we already pay for?
Does this need to be a separate event at all?

name: Anti-weight
ess: If something is too heavy to carry, pair it with something that lifts.
subs: Compensate weight by joining with something that provides lift
Compensate weight by interaction with the environment
mfg: Counterweight on a crane jib
Buoyancy or air support for heavy handling
svc: Fund a new control by deleting the one it supersedes, rather than adding it on top and calling the total a process
Let the part of the system that gains carry the cost: the team that benefits from clean data does the validation at the point of entry
Offset a seasonal trough with counter-seasonal demand rather than flexing headcount against it
Pair a burdensome disclosure with the moment the customer receives the discount, so the weight is carried by something they want
Let an established partner's platform carry the credibility a new service has not yet earned
ask: What part of the system gains from this, and could it carry the cost instead of the part that bears it now?
What could carry the weight of this burden for us?
Is there an opposing force in the environment we can borrow rather than fight?
What does the customer actually want, that we could attach this to?

name: Preliminary anti-action
ess: If an action will cause harm, apply the opposite in advance.
subs: Apply a counter-action in advance of a harmful action
Create stresses in advance that oppose the stresses to come
mfg: Pre-stressed concrete and pre-tensioned bolts
Pre-cool a part that is about to be heated
svc: Before a price rise, deliver a visible improvement first so goodwill is already banked
Deliberately set a low expectation before a phase you know is painful — 'this will take six weeks, here is why'
Pre-empt the three objections you know are coming, inside the proposal itself
Brief the frontline before the campaign lands, so the first complaint is not the first they hear of it
Build a small deliberate buffer of goodwill or budget ahead of a known-disruptive change
ask: What harm will this action cause — can we apply its opposite beforehand?
What could we say or do first that absorbs the coming shock?
Who will be hit hardest, and what could we give them in advance?

name: Preliminary action
ess: Do it before it is needed, and set things up so the moment itself is trivial.
subs: Perform the required change before it is needed
Pre-arrange things so they can act without losing time waiting
mfg: Pre-drilled and pre-tapped components
Kitting all parts to the line before the shift starts
svc: Pre-fill every form field with data you already hold, and ask only for what is genuinely new
Pre-approve a credit limit so the customer's application is a confirmation, not an assessment
Prepare theatre packs and case notes the night before the list
Book the follow-up appointment at the end of the current one, while the person is still in front of you
Have the contract, the onboarding pack and the first invoice drafted before the deal is signed
ask: What could be done before the customer arrives — or before the clock starts?
What information are we asking for that we already hold?
What would make the actual moment of service take thirty seconds?

name: Beforehand cushioning
ess: Assume it will fail, and put the remedy in place now.
subs: Prepare emergency means beforehand to compensate for relatively low reliability
mfg: Standby power and spare tooling on the shelf
Safety stock ahead of a known-fragile supply
svc: A standing surge rota that activates on a defined trigger, not on a manager's judgement
Hold a capacity buffer sized to the variation you actually see, not to the average you report
A service-recovery budget frontline staff can spend without asking anyone
Pre-written holding statements and comms for the four incidents you know will recur
A named deputy for every single-point-of-failure role, exercised not just nominated
Pre-agreed escalation route with the supplier, signed before you need it
ask: What will go wrong here, and what is already in place for when it does?
Can we pre-authorise the fix so nobody has to ask permission mid-crisis?
Where is our single point of failure, and what is the standby?

name: Equipotentiality
ess: Change the conditions so nothing has to be lifted up and down at all.
subs: Change operating conditions to eliminate the need to raise or lower
mfg: Transfer between machines at a single common height
Roller decks that remove all lifting from the operation
svc: Give frontline staff the authority to decide, so nothing has to be lifted to a manager and back
One shared record so information is never re-keyed from one system into another
Keep the customer in a single channel rather than transferring them between three teams
Flatten a three-stage sign-off to one, with sampling instead of serial approval
Bring the decision-maker to the work rather than sending the work up to the decision-maker
ask: Where are we lifting things up and down levels — approvals, hand-offs, re-keying?
Could the decision be made where the work actually happens?
What would have to be true for this never to need escalation?

name: The other way round
ess: Invert it. Do the opposite, or swap who moves and who stays still.
subs: Invert the action used to solve the problem
Make movable parts fixed, and fixed parts movable
Turn the object upside down
mfg: Move the workpiece past a fixed tool instead of the tool past the work
Rotate the assembly rather than the operator
svc: Instead of the customer coming to the service, send the service to them — mobile clinics, home visits, field engineers
Instead of chasing customers for a document, redesign so the document is not needed
Instead of training people to use a complicated system, simplify it until training is unnecessary
Let the customer serve themselves and have staff supervise the exceptions, rather than the reverse
Instead of forecasting demand and building capacity, shape the demand to fit the capacity you have
ask: What if we did the exact opposite of what we do now?
Who else could do this — the customer, the supplier, the system?
Which part should be moving, and which should be standing still?

name: Spheroidality — curvature
ess: Trade straight lines for curves, and linear motion for rotation.
subs: Replace linear parts with curved, flat surfaces with spherical
Use rollers, balls, spirals, domes
Replace linear motion with rotary; use centrifugal force
mfg: Ball bearings and roller conveyors instead of sliding
Spiral accumulators to buffer product without a long straight run
svc: Replace a linear stage-gate programme with a short repeating loop that revisits the same questions
Replace a linear escalation ladder with a loop that returns the case to the same owner, so nothing is handed away and forgotten
Circulate work around a small cell where everyone can pick it up, rather than passing it down a line
Rotate duties on a cycle instead of fixing people in posts
Replace sequential sign-off with one round-table where all parties decide together
A recurring review rhythm rather than a one-off launch and hope
ask: Does this really have to be a straight line from A to B?
Would a loop beat a sequence here — coming round again rather than getting it right once?
What could be made to rotate rather than travel?

name: Dynamics
ess: Make the fixed things adjustable, so they can be optimal at every stage.
subs: Allow characteristics to change to be optimal at each stage
Divide into elements that can change relative position
If rigid, make it movable or adaptive
mfg: Variable-speed drives and adjustable jigs
Tooling that reconfigures between variants without a changeover
svc: Staff to the demand curve hour by hour rather than a fixed shift pattern
Pricing that flexes by time, channel or load
A policy with an adjustable threshold rather than one fixed rule set annually
A conversation script that branches on the customer's answers instead of running fixed
Team composition that changes across the phases of a project
ask: What is fixed today that could flex with conditions?
What would 'adjustable' look like here — and who would turn the dial?
Are we optimised for an average that never actually occurs?

name: Partial or excessive actions
ess: If you cannot have exactly 100%, take slightly less or slightly more — it is usually easier.
subs: If 100% is hard to achieve, do slightly less or slightly more and simplify the problem
mfg: Overspray then wipe back to a clean edge
Overfill and level rather than dose precisely
svc: Send the imperfect draft early rather than the perfect one late
Let 80% of the volume run straight through on a rule and hold only the exceptions for judgement
Pay 90% of the claim immediately and investigate only the disputed remainder
Deliberately over-staff the first week of a launch, then taper
Give a partial answer now with a committed follow-up, instead of silence until you are certain
Approve everything under a threshold without checks, and check hard above it
ask: Is 'all or nothing' really the constraint, or just habit?
What does 80% now buy us that 100% later does not?
Would deliberately overshooting be cheaper than hitting it exactly?

name: Another dimension
ess: If it will not work in one dimension, add another.
subs: Move into two or three dimensions instead of one
Use a multi-storey arrangement instead of a single layer
Tilt or re-orient the object
Use the other side of a given area
mfg: Vertical carousel storage instead of floor racking
Multi-level conveyors crossing over each other
svc: Triage on two axes — urgency and complexity — instead of a single priority number
Segment the queue on a second attribute — complexity as well as urgency — so one dimension cannot dominate the routing
Add an asynchronous channel alongside the live one, so the queue is not the only dimension
Move a meeting into a shared document, where people contribute in parallel rather than in turn
Use the back of the appointment card, the footer of the receipt, the space you already own
Segment the customer base by behaviour as well as by value
ask: What second axis are we ignoring in this decision?
Could this happen in a different plane — asynchronous instead of live, written instead of spoken?
What surface do we already have that we are not using?

name: Mechanical vibration
ess: Oscillate it. Raise the frequency. Find the natural rhythm and ride it.
subs: Cause the object to oscillate
Increase the frequency, up to ultrasonic
Use resonant frequency
Use piezoelectric instead of mechanical vibrators
mfg: Vibratory bowl feeders that orient parts automatically
Ultrasonic cleaning reaching where brushes cannot
svc: Release work into the process in small, frequent batches rather than one weekly drop, so the queue never has to absorb a spike
Sample continuously at low volume instead of running a large periodic audit that finds problems long after they were made
Replace the annual engagement survey with a weekly two-question pulse
Many small nudges beat one big campaign — raise the frequency, lower the amplitude
Match the customer's own rhythm — bill when they get paid, contact them when they are free — that is resonance
ask: Would more, smaller, more frequent beats work better than one big event?
What natural rhythm does the customer or the work already have, that we could ride?
What are we doing annually that ought to be weekly?

name: Periodic action
ess: Stop doing it continuously. Pulse it — and use the gaps.
subs: Replace continuous action with periodic or pulsed action
If already periodic, change the frequency
Use pauses between impulses to perform another action
mfg: Pulsed welding to control heat input
Intermittent lubrication rather than constant flow
svc: Batch interruptions — handle email in three defined windows rather than continuously
Batch the arrival of work rather than the work itself: fixed release times smooth the queue without changing a single step
Published 'office hours' for internal support instead of always-on availability
Scheduled release trains instead of continuous unplanned change
Use the quiet periods deliberately for improvement work, training and maintenance
Concentrate outbound calling into blocks so the rest of the day is uninterrupted
ask: Does this genuinely have to be continuous?
What useful thing could we do in the pauses?
Would a defined rhythm protect the work better than constant availability?

name: Continuity of useful action
ess: Never let the valuable thing sit idle.
subs: Work continuously, with all parts always at full load
Remove idle and intermediate motion
mfg: Lights-out running of the bottleneck machine
Eliminating machine idle during changeover with external set-up
svc: Keep the case moving on everything that does not depend on the missing input, rather than stopping the whole file
Decouple two steps with a small deliberate buffer, so a stoppage in one does not idle the other
Use the customer's waiting time for something useful — complete the details while they wait
Follow-the-sun coverage so work progresses across time zones overnight
Remove the queue between two steps so work never rests between them
Keep the scarce expert working on scarce-expert problems only
ask: Where does work sit still — and would a buffer there stop one stoppage idling everything downstream?
Can something useful happen during that wait?
Is our most expensive resource ever idle — or ever doing cheap work?

name: Skipping
ess: If a stage is harmful mainly because it lasts, go through it fast.
subs: Conduct a process, or certain stages of it, at high speed
mfg: High-speed cutting that removes material before heat can build up
Flash heating or rapid quench to skip an unwanted phase
svc: Cut the number of stages a case passes through rather than speeding each one up — the harm lives in the dwell time between stages, not in the work
Time-box a stage hard and let it complete with what it has, rather than letting it expand to fill the time available
A single two-hour decision session instead of six weeks of circulated email
A big-bang cutover rather than a long, expensive period of dual running
Push a change through while the window is open, rather than consulting it to death
ask: Which stage is harmful mainly because of how long a case sits in it, rather than how long the work takes?
What if we did it so fast that the harm never had time to develop?
What are we drawing out that we should be ripping off?

name: Blessing in disguise
ess: Turn the harm into the resource. Make lemons into lemonade.
subs: Use harmful factors to achieve a positive effect
Eliminate a harmful factor by combining it with another harmful factor
Amplify a harmful factor until it stops being harmful
mfg: Recover waste heat to preheat incoming material
Use process scrap as feedstock for a lower grade product
svc: Treat complaints as your best-funded, most honest source of improvement ideas — and say so publicly
Use the outage as the forcing event that finally retires the legacy process
Let a backlog of waiting customers become the test population for a new channel
Use peak demand as the business case that unlocks automation funding
A visible, well-handled failure can build more trust than a service that never failed
ask: What harm here could become a resource if we turned it round?
Which two problems, put together, might cancel each other out?
What is this failure giving us that success never would?

name: Feedback
ess: Close the loop — and if there is a loop already, change its speed or strength.
subs: Introduce feedback to improve a process or action
If feedback already exists, change its magnitude or influence
mfg: Closed-loop process control and statistical process control
In-line gauging that adjusts the machine automatically
svc: Shorten the loop rather than enlarging the report: a signal the same day beats a dashboard next month
Tell the person who took the decision what happened as a result — most frontline staff never find out
Close the loop with the customer after a complaint: what changed because of you
Live queue and wait-time displays that let people self-regulate
Change the loop from a monthly report to a same-day signal, and watch behaviour change
Feed audit findings back to the team that generated them, not only upwards
ask: Who acts here, and do they ever learn what happened?
How fast is the loop — could it be same-day instead of monthly?
Is the feedback going to the people with the power to act on it?

name: Intermediary
ess: Put something in between — and let it disappear once the job is done.
subs: Use an intermediary carrier or intermediary process
Merge one object temporarily with another that is easily removed
mfg: Carriers and pallets that take the part through the process
Sacrificial layers and temporary coatings
svc: A named case coordinator who owns the customer across every hand-off
A translation layer between two systems that cannot talk to each other, rather than replacing either
A broker, aggregator or comparison service that stands between supply and demand
A neutral facilitator for a contentious decision between two departments
A transitional account manager who holds the relationship through a migration, then steps away
ask: Who or what could carry this across the gap?
Is there a temporary go-between that could be removed later?
Would an intermediary be cheaper than making the two ends fit?

name: Self-service
ess: Make it serve itself, and make its by-products do work.
subs: Make an object serve itself by performing auxiliary helpful functions
Use waste resources, energy or substances
mfg: Self-lubricating bearings and self-cleaning filters
Using process off-cuts to fire the plant
svc: Customer self-service for the routine 80%, with humans reserved for the exceptions
Teams that inspect their own work instead of a separate QA gate downstream
A process that produces its own audit trail as a by-product of doing the work
Peer-to-peer support communities where customers answer each other
Use data you already generate for free as the input to the next improvement
ask: What could this do for itself, without us?
What by-product of the work could be fed straight back into the work?
Why is there a separate function doing something the doer could do?

name: Copying
alias: Use a copy, not the original
ess: Do not use the expensive original when a cheap copy will do.
subs: Use a simple, inexpensive copy instead of a fragile or expensive object
Replace an object with optical copies, at a suitable scale
If visible copies are used, move to infrared or ultraviolet
mfg: Digital twin used for trials instead of stopping the real line
Master gauge copied to cheap working gauges
svc: Simulate the redesigned process on paper or in a model before rebuilding anything
Record the expert once, instead of booking the expert forty times
Train on a masked copy of live data rather than on live data itself
Mystery-shop your own journey to see the copy the customer actually experiences
Templates and worked examples instead of drafting each document from scratch
ask: Do we need the real thing here, or would a copy, model or recording do?
Who is a scarce original that we should be copying?
What could we test on a replica before we touch production?

name: Cheap short-living objects
ess: Replace one expensive, durable thing with many cheap, disposable ones.
subs: Replace an expensive object with several cheap ones, giving up some qualities such as longevity
mfg: Disposable tooling and single-use consumables
Cheap cardboard fixtures for a short production run
svc: Run ten cheap disposable experiments instead of one large irreversible programme
A pop-up desk or temporary site to test a location before signing a lease
Throwaway landing pages to test demand before building the service
Short-term contracted capacity for a known spike, rather than permanent headcount
A deliberately temporary policy with a built-in expiry date
ask: What are we over-engineering for permanence that could be deliberately disposable?
Could we learn the same thing with something cheap and throwaway?
What are we committing to for years that we only need for weeks?

name: Mechanics substitution
alias: Replace the thing with a signal
ess: Replace the physical mechanism with an informational or sensory one.
subs: Replace a mechanical means with a sensory means
Use electric, magnetic or electromagnetic fields to interact
Replace static fields with moving, structured or time-varying ones
Use fields in conjunction with responsive particles
mfg: Electronic control replacing a mechanical linkage
Magnetic clamping instead of bolts and clamps
svc: Digital signature replacing the posted, wet-signed form
An automated nudge replacing the manual chase call
A virtual queue — go away, we will text you — replacing the physical one
Sensors and dashboards replacing supervisory walk-rounds
A rule in the system replacing a paragraph in a policy nobody reads
ask: Which physical or manual mechanism could be replaced by an information one?
What if the 'thing' became a signal?
Where are we moving atoms when we could be moving bits?

name: Pneumatics and hydraulics
ess: Use something that flows and cushions instead of something rigid.
subs: Replace solid parts with gas or liquid ones — inflatable, hydrostatic, air cushion
mfg: Air-cushion transport for heavy or delicate loads
Hydraulic clamping that self-equalises across an uneven surface
svc: A flexible pool of on-call or bank staff that inflates at peak and deflates after
A levelling buffer of work released at a steady rate, smoothing flow rather than rigid daily targets
Budget held centrally as 'float' that flows to wherever the pressure is
Cash-flow float or a facility that cushions the shock instead of a rigid payment schedule
Cloud-style elastic capacity rather than owned fixed capacity
ask: What could be made fluid rather than solid here — capacity, budget, roles, rules?
Where do we need a cushion that inflates only when the pressure comes?
What is rigid because nobody has questioned it?

name: Flexible shells and thin films
ess: A thin flexible layer can do the job of a heavy structure.
subs: Use flexible shells and thin films instead of three-dimensional structures
Isolate the object from its environment with flexible shells and thin films
mfg: Shrink wrap replacing a rigid crate
Membranes and liners protecting a vessel instead of thicker walls
svc: A lightweight digital wrapper over a legacy system, instead of a multi-year replacement
A one-page policy summary that fronts a hundred pages of detailed rules
A simple front-end experience over a complicated back office — the customer never sees the machinery
Ring-fence a risky pilot inside a thin governance boundary so it can move fast without endangering the core
A thin service layer that lets partners integrate without exposing your internals
ask: Could a thin layer do the job of the heavy structure we are planning?
What needs a membrane around it rather than a wall?
Can we wrap this rather than replace it?

name: Porous materials
ess: Build in deliberate gaps — then use them.
subs: Make an object porous, or add porous elements
If already porous, fill the pores with a useful substance
mfg: Sintered porous filters and vacuum chucks
Porous carriers used to introduce a lubricant exactly where needed
svc: Deliberately plan schedules to less than 100% so the system can absorb variation instead of collapsing at the first delay
Permeable team boundaries that let information and people flow between them
Open days, secondments and embedded customers — deliberate holes in the organisational wall
Then fill those gaps with something useful: improvement work, training, cover, thinking time
Slack in the timetable that absorbs the emergency case without cancelling the routine list
ask: Is our system too solid to absorb ordinary variation?
What deliberate gaps would let things flow — and what should fill them?
Are we running at 100% utilisation and calling the resulting chaos bad luck?

name: Colour changes
alias: Make it obvious at a glance
ess: Change what can be seen, and by whom.
subs: Change the colour of an object or its surroundings
Change the transparency of an object or its surroundings
Use coloured additives or luminescent tracers to observe hard-to-see things
mfg: Colour-coded parts and tooling that make the wrong one obvious
UV tracer dye to find a leak
svc: Red-amber-green visual boards that show status at a glance, with no report required
Colour-coded triage bands, wristbands or file covers that carry the instruction without words
Make pricing genuinely transparent as a competitive weapon
Publish the backlog and the wait time — change who can see it, and behaviour changes
Add a visible marker to the cases that have been waiting longest, so they cannot be quietly ignored
ask: What is invisible here that ought to be obvious at a glance?
Could colour or position carry the instruction instead of text?
Who currently cannot see this, and what would change if they could?

name: Homogeneity
ess: Let things interact with things of their own kind.
subs: Make objects interact with objects of the same material, or of similar properties
mfg: Same-material joints so the assembly can be recycled whole
Matching thermal properties to stop differential movement
svc: One shared data standard end to end, so nothing has to be translated between teams
One identifier for a customer across every system, so records never have to be matched or de-duplicated
One vocabulary across departments — the same word meaning the same thing in ops, finance and sales
Match the adviser to the customer's language, sector or circumstance
Use the same tool and format from intake to closure, rather than converting at each stage
Recruit for the same underlying capability across a team so work can move freely within it
ask: Where do mismatches — of format, language, system or culture — create friction?
What would 'same nature' look like across this hand-off?
How many translations does one piece of information go through here?

name: Discarding and recovering
ess: Design things to disappear when their job is done — and to renew themselves while running.
subs: Discard, dissolve or evaporate portions that have completed their function
Restore consumable parts during operation
mfg: Dissolvable cores and consumable fixtures
Automatic tool replenishment without stopping the machine
svc: Put an expiry date on every new rule and control, so it dies unless actively renewed
Task forces that are chartered to disband on a fixed date
Remove a control once the risk it was created for has genuinely passed
Replenish trained staff continuously through a rolling programme rather than periodic campaigns
Retire the temporary workaround at the same moment the permanent fix lands — plan it in
ask: What should have been switched off by now, and why is it still running?
What could be designed to expire on its own?
What is being consumed here that should be replenished continuously rather than in bursts?

name: Parameter changes
ess: Turn a dial. Change a setting rather than the design.
subs: Change the physical state
Change the concentration or consistency
Change the degree of flexibility
Change the temperature or volume
mfg: Change viscosity, concentration or temperature rather than redesign the process
Change batch size to change everything downstream
svc: Change the concentration of an intervention — four deep sessions rather than twenty light ones
Change the temperature of a dispute by moving it from a live call to a written exchange
Change the degree of flexibility in a rule — from mandatory to advisory, or the reverse
Change the batch size of work released to a team, and the queue behaves completely differently
Change the formality of a meeting and you change who really speaks
ask: Which dial could we simply turn — size, frequency, concentration, flexibility, formality?
Are we redesigning something when we could just change a setting?
What happens at half the batch size, or twice the frequency?

name: Phase transitions
